title: Task/update full discover UI
summary: Since the last plan (commit `c947d26`), tapping a note marker in the Bible text now switches the Discover panel back to the **Notes** chip when another chip was selected, so the note is shown and highlighted. Two tests that failed last time were rewritten, because the earlier plan expected the wrong thing. Overall, the full **Discover** side panel (opened from the toolbar) now looks the same as the smaller Discover panel that sits beside the Bible text: the same "Discover <book>" header, the same **+ Create** button, and the same row of filter chips. Its close (X) button now sits in that header, and the create-note, create-playlist and play-playlist screens inside the panel each get the same style of header with a back arrow and a close button. Friends' playlists still appear in the full panel and get their own **Friends' playlists** filter chip.

links.label: Issue 2000: Update the full discover panel to use the same design as the compact discover panel

setup.title: Open the preview build
setup.body: Use Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a computer (a phone is only needed for the last section). Open the preview link above. If it shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload. If the page looks like an older version, do a hard refresh: Ctrl+Shift+R (Windows) or Cmd+Shift+R (Mac).

setup.title: Sign in
setup.body: Sign in with your email address. You'll get a code by email, so use an inbox you can check. Several tests create notes and playlists, which need you to be signed in.

setup.title: Make the window wide
setup.body: Make your browser window as wide as your screen allows (at least about 1100 pixels wide), so the side panel can open beside the Bible text.

setup.title: Know where the Discover button is
setup.body: The full Discover panel opens from the **Discover** button (a compass icon) in the reader's toolbar. If you don't see it, look in the toolbar's overflow (more) menu.

tests.title: The full panel has the new header, + Create button and close button
tests.why: Failed on the plan for commit `c947d26`: John 3 had no content for the tester, so the panel showed the notes section with **Create a note** and no filter chips. That is the intended behavior (there's nothing to filter), so the plan's expectation was wrong, not the app. This test now checks only the header; the chips are checked in the filter test below. This is the main change asked for in issue 2000: the full panel should look like the small panel beside the text.
steps: Open **John 3**.
Select the **Discover** (compass) button in the toolbar.
expected: A side panel opens with a compass icon and the title **Discover John** at the top.
To the right of the title is a **+ Create** button, followed by an **X** close button.
There is no second, separate header bar above it (only one title row, not two).

Below the header is either a row of filter chips starting with **All** (when the chapter has more than one kind of content), or, if John 3 has nothing to show for you, a notes section with a **Create a note** button and no chips. Both are correct.

tests.title: The panel's X button closes it
steps: With the Discover panel open, select the **X** at the top right of the panel.
expected: The Discover panel closes and the Bible text takes the full width again.

tests.title: + Create offers both Annotation and Playlist
steps: Open the Discover panel again.
Select **+ Create**.
expected: A small menu opens with two choices: **Annotation** and **Playlist**.

tests.title: Filter chips switch what the panel shows
tests.before: Use a chapter that has cross references or study notes, such as **John 3**. If you have a note on this chapter, even better. Chips only appear when the chapter has at least two kinds of content. If no chapter you try shows chips, mark this test Blocked and come back to it after the Friends' playlists section, where a friend's playlist adds a chip.
steps: In the Discover panel, look at the chips under the header.
Select each chip in turn (for example **Notes**, **Cross references**, **Study notes**), then select **All** again.
expected: Each chip shows only its own kind of content, and the chip you picked looks selected.
**All** shows everything again.
If there are more chips than fit, small arrow buttons let you scroll the chip row left and right.

tests.title: A chapter with nothing to show still shows a useful panel
tests.why: The full panel is meant to never be blank: when the chapter has nothing to show, the empty Notes section with a **Create a note** prompt takes its place.
tests.before: Pick a chapter you have no notes on and that's unlikely to have study material, for example **Obadiah 1** or **3 John 1**. If it turns out to have cross references, try another short book until one shows nothing but notes.
steps: Open that chapter with the Discover panel open.
expected: The panel still shows its header (**Discover <book name>**, **+ Create**, **X**).
Below it is a notes section saying "You don't have any notes for this chapter." with a **Create a note** button, not an empty white panel.

tests.title: The panel follows the selected tab and chapter
steps: With the Discover panel open, go to the next chapter using the toolbar's next-chapter arrow.
If you have more than one reading tab open, switch to another tab.
expected: The panel title changes to match the book you're now reading (for example **Discover Romans**) and its content changes to the new chapter.

sections.title: Creating and playing from the panel
sections.intro: Each screen inside the Discover panel now has its own header with a back arrow and a close button.

tests.title: Creating an annotation shows a back arrow, a title and a close button
steps: Open **John 3** and open the Discover panel.
Select **+ Create**, then **Annotation**.
expected: The panel shows a header with a back arrow, a title starting with **Annotate** followed by the place in the Bible (for example **Annotate John 3**), and an **X** close button on the right.
Below it is the note editor with a **Save** button.

tests.title: Saving an annotation returns to the Discover view and shows the note
steps: In the annotation editor, type `Testing the new Discover panel`.
Select **Save**.
expected: A message like **Annotation saved** appears.
The panel goes back to **Discover John** and your note appears under the notes section.

tests.title: The back arrow on the annotation screen goes back without saving
steps: Select **+ Create**, then **Annotation**.
Type `Do not save me`.
Select the back arrow at the top left of the panel.
expected: The panel returns to the **Discover John** view.
No note with the text "Do not save me" appears.

tests.title: Creating a playlist shows the title box, back arrow and close button in the header
steps: Select **+ Create**, then **Playlist**.
expected: The panel header shows a back arrow, a text box with the placeholder **Playlist title**, and an **X** close button.
If an AI assistant is available in your account, a sparkle (AI) button also appears in the header.
Below the header are the cover image and item sections of the playlist form.

tests.title: The back arrow on an unsaved playlist asks before throwing it away
steps: Type `Discover test playlist` in the **Playlist title** box.
Select the back arrow.
expected: A box appears saying you have unsaved changes and asking what you'd like to do.
Choosing to keep editing leaves you on the playlist form with your title still there.

tests.title: Saving a playlist and playing it
steps: Still on the playlist form, add one item: a Bible passage such as `John 3:16`, following the form's prompts.
Select **Save**.
Open your profile (your picture or account icon), select **Your content**, then the **Playlists** chip.
Find **Discover test playlist** and play it.
expected: While playing, the Discover panel header shows a back arrow, the playlist title **Discover test playlist**, and an **X** close button.
Selecting the back arrow returns to the previous view.
tests.why: Failed on the plan for commit `c947d26`: the tester couldn't find their own playlist in the Discover panel. The Discover panel only lists friends' playlists, and it did before this PR too; your own playlists are under **Your content**. The steps now say where to look.

tests.title: Closing the panel while a playlist plays stops it
tests.why: Closing used to go through the panel's old header; the new X button is meant to behave the same way.
steps: Play the playlist again.
Select the **X** at the top right of the panel.
expected: The panel closes and the playlist stops playing.
Opening the Discover panel again shows the normal **Discover <book>** view, not the playing playlist.

setup.title: You need a friend with a playlist
setup.body: Skip this section (mark the tests Skip) if you can't set this up. Otherwise, use a second account that is your friend in Seed Bible and has at least one playlist. You can create one by signing in with a different email address in a private/incognito window, making a playlist there, and adding each other as friends.

tests.title: Friends' playlists appear in the full panel with their own chip
steps: In your main account, open the Discover panel on any chapter.
expected: A **Friends' playlists** chip appears in the filter row.
Under **All**, a section titled **Playlists from your friends** lists your friend's name and picture with their playlists below.
Selecting the **Friends' playlists** chip shows only that section.

tests.title: Friends' playlists do not appear in the small panel beside the text
tests.before: Turn on **Settings** → **Discovered Content** → **Show discovered content**, and close the Discover side panel.
steps: Open a chapter that has notes or cross references, so the small Discover panel appears beside or below the Bible text.
expected: The small panel has the same header and chip style, but no **Friends' playlists** chip or section.

tests.title: Tapping a note marker in the text switches the panel back to your notes
tests.why: New since commit `c947d26`. The earlier code review found that tapping a note marker did nothing while another chip (such as **Friends' playlists** or **Cross references**) was selected, and the panel jumped to the note later when you switched back to **All**. The panel now switches to the **Notes** chip right away.
tests.before: You need a note on the chapter (the one saved earlier on **John 3** works) and a chip other than **All** and **Notes** in the full panel. The **Friends' playlists** chip from the previous tests is fine; so is **Cross references** if it shows.
steps: Open **John 3** with the full Discover panel open.
Select the **Friends' playlists** chip (or **Cross references**). Your note is no longer listed.
In the Bible text, select the note marker beside the verse that has your note.
expected: The panel switches to the **Notes** chip on its own, and the chip looks selected.
Your note is scrolled into view and briefly highlighted.
Selecting **All** afterwards does not make the list jump to the note again.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: The small panel beside the text still works, and only creates annotations
tests.before: **Settings** → **Discovered Content** → **Show discovered content** is on, and the Discover side panel is closed.
steps: Open **John 3**.
Look at the small **Discover John** panel beside or below the Bible text.
Select its **+ Create** button.
expected: The small panel has no **X** close button.
**+ Create** goes straight to the annotation editor without a menu (no Playlist choice).

tests.title: Opening the full panel hides the small one
steps: With the small panel visible, select the **Discover** button in the toolbar.
expected: The full panel opens on the side and the small panel next to the text disappears, so the same content isn't shown twice.
Closing the full panel with its **X** brings the small panel back.

tests.title: Dark mode
steps: Switch the app to dark mode in **Settings**.
Open the Discover panel, then the annotation and playlist screens.
expected: The header, chips, buttons and text are all readable on the dark background, with nothing left white or invisible.

tests.title: On a phone, Discover opens full screen with a working close button
tests.before: Use a phone, or make your computer's browser window very narrow (about the width of a phone).
steps: Open the Discover panel from the toolbar.
Select **+ Create**, then **Annotation**, then the back arrow.
Select the **X**.
expected: The panel fills the screen and shows the **Discover <book>** header, **+ Create** and **X** without overlapping or being cut off.
The back arrow returns to the Discover view, and **X** closes the panel and shows the Bible text again.

notCovered: Moving the Discover code into a new folder and deleting the old one is internal and has no visible effect beyond what's tested above.
Some English text entries were reordered in the translation file; the words themselves didn't change.

In the old full panel, extra content types added by extensions had sections you could fold away. Those fold-away sections were removed; extension content now shows behind filter chips instead. This is only testable with an extension that adds content to Discover.

The same note-marker fix also applies to the small panel beside the text, but reaching it there needs a chapter with a note plus other content behind chips, so it's only tested in the full panel. Unit tests cover it.

This commit also brings in unrelated changes merged from the main branch (the desktop toolbar can now show a fourth tool instead of **More** when it fits). Those belong to another pull request and aren't tested here.
